headline: Bangladesh plans to buy Chinese J-10CE fighter jets
summary: A draft agreement is already prepared as the government eyes the multirole fighter for its performance and cost-effectiveness.
details: The Bangladesh government is moving forward with plans to purchase J-10CE fighter jets from China, according to Information and Broadcasting Adviser Zahed Ur Rahman.
Speaking at a press conference on Tuesday, the adviser revealed that a draft agreement for the acquisition has already been prepared.
Zahed Ur Rahman highlighted the aircraft's combat performance, claiming that the J-10CE has performed well in real combat situations against advanced 4.5 generation fighters like the Rafale.
The adviser also noted that Chinese fighter jets are significantly more affordable than European variants of similar quality, such as the Rafale or Eurofighter Typhoon.
The move is part of the government's effort to modernize its air defense capabilities with cost-effective and high-performance aircraft.
caption:
Bangladesh is eyeing China's J-10CE fighter jets for its air force. A draft agreement is already in the works.

The Bangladesh government is moving forward with plans to purchase J-10CE fighter jets from China, according to Information and Broadcasting Adviser Zahed Ur Rahman.

Speaking at a press conference on Tuesday, the adviser revealed that a draft agreement for the acquisition has already been prepared.

Zahed Ur Rahman highlighted the aircraft's combat performance, claiming that the J-10CE has performed well in real combat situations against advanced 4.5 generation fighters like the Rafale.

The adviser also noted that Chinese fighter jets are significantly more affordable than European variants of similar quality, such as the Rafale or Eurofighter Typhoon.

The move is part of the government's effort to modernize its air defense capabilities with cost-effective and high-performance aircraft.

headline: 943 deaths this year as 5 more die with measles-like symptoms in 24 hours
summary: The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) reports a surge in suspected measles cases, with nearly 1,000 new suspected infections in a single day.
details: Five patients died with measles-like symptoms within a 24-hour window ending today at 8:00 am. This brings the total number of confirmed and suspected measles-related deaths in Bangladesh to 943 this year.
The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) has classified all five of the most recent fatalities as suspected measles deaths.
Currently, the total number of suspected measles deaths stands at 844, while laboratory-confirmed deaths remain at 99.
In the last 24 hours alone, 986 new suspected measles cases were reported, pushing the nationwide cumulative total of suspected cases to 151,638.
Additionally, 91 new confirmed measles cases were recorded, bringing the total number of laboratory-confirmed infections to 18,578.
Since March 15 of this year, 132,554 patients with suspected measles have been hospitalized across the country, of whom 127,811 have recovered, according to DGHS data.
